title: Microsoft Launches Project Perception, an AI Security Platform That Pits Red and Blue Team Agents Against Each Other
excerpt: The platform deploys more than 100 specialised AI agents to hunt vulnerabilities, backed by a new security model Microsoft claims outperforms GPT and Gemini on cyber benchmarks.
body:
• Microsoft launched Project Perception, an agentic AI platform that coordinates Red Team, Blue Team and Green Team AI agents to continuously detect, analyse and fix security vulnerabilities.
  • The platform is built around MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, Microsoft's first dedicated cybersecurity AI model, which the company claims outperforms competing models from Google and OpenAI on industry benchmarks.
  • The underlying system, codenamed MDASH, has already discovered 16 previously unknown vulnerabilities in Windows networking components, including four critical remote code execution flaws.
  • Microsoft says the platform reduces operational costs by nearly 50 percent compared to using general-purpose frontier models for security analysis.

How Project Perception Works

Microsoft has launched Project Perception, an AI-powered cybersecurity platform that takes a fundamentally different approach from conventional security tools. Instead of relying on a single AI model, the platform coordinates more than 100 specialised AI agents organised into three teams.

https://x.com/financespotnews/status/2081850542792360021

"The underlying system, codenamed MDASH, has already discovered 16 previously unknown vulnerabilities in Windows networking components, including four critical remote code execution flaws."

Red Team agents proactively hunt for vulnerabilities, simulating the techniques real attackers would use to find exploitable weaknesses. Blue Team agents analyse alerts and investigate suspicious activity, determining which threats need immediate attention. Green Team agents recommend or implement fixes after customer approval, closing the loop from detection to remediation.

The system routes tasks across AI models from Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, using a model-selection layer that reserves expensive frontier model calls for high-value analysis and assigns cheaper, distilled models to routine scanning. Microsoft says this architecture cuts operational costs by nearly half compared to running everything on frontier models.

A Purpose-Built Security Model

At the core of Project Perception is MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, Microsoft's first AI model built exclusively for cybersecurity. The company claims the model delivers better vulnerability detection than competing models from Google (Gemini) and OpenAI (ChatGPT) on industry cybersecurity benchmarks, including an 88.45 percent score on the CyberGym benchmark covering more than 1,500 real-world vulnerabilities.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=V5qqmHBhYac

The model builds on MDASH (Microsoft Security multi-model agentic scanning harness), an internal system that has already found 16 previously unknown vulnerabilities in Windows networking and authentication components. Four critical flaws — including remote code execution bugs in the TCP/IP stack and IKEv2 service — were patched in a recent Patch Tuesday release.

The Competitive Landscape

Project Perception enters a market where AI-driven vulnerability discovery is rapidly becoming the standard. Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview is currently considered the most capable vulnerability-hunting AI, but its access is restricted and expensive. Microsoft is positioning Project Perception as a more accessible and affordable alternative for enterprise security teams.

The platform was developed under Hayete Gallot, the executive vice president for security who returned to Microsoft from Google Cloud in February 2026. Since her arrival, she has reorganised Microsoft's security business around AI products.

The launch comes days after Nvidia formed the Open Secure AI Alliance, a coalition of 37 companies including SpaceX, Microsoft and Palantir that aims to build open-source AI cybersecurity tools. The parallel initiatives reflect a broader industry push to weaponise AI for defence as cyberattacks become faster and more automated.
nri_angle: Indian-origin tech professionals hold senior cybersecurity roles across Microsoft and its enterprise clients, and the platform signals a shift in how security teams will work with AI.
